subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Green Defaults
description: A quick win: understand Green Defaults.

hook.text: A utility switched the default electricity plan from standard to renewable.

buildup.text: Green defaults make the sustainable option the path of least resistance. Most people accept whatever is pre-selected.

discovery.text: Pichert and Katsikopoulos showed green defaults work even when the green option costs slightly more.

twist.text: When people discover they were defaulted into a costlier plan, backlash can erase gains.

climax.text: Green defaults combined with clear disclosure balance effectiveness and trust.

punchline.text: Make green the default and most people stay green.

quiz.question: What risk do green defaults carry?
options: They always cost significantly more than standard options
Backlash if people discover they were defaulted into a costlier plan without knowing

details.summary: Green defaults set environmentally friendly options as the pre-selected choice, such as double-sided printing, renewable energy plans, or paperless billing. Since most people accept defaults, green defaults shift large populations toward sustainable behavior without any mandate.
details.whyItMatters: Green defaults leverage inertia for environmental benefit, converting the behavioral tendency to accept pre-selected options into a force for sustainability. They achieve mass behavior change at near-zero cost and without limiting freedom.
takeaways: Green defaults convert inertia into pro-environmental behavior at scale
Renewable energy uptake jumps from under 10 to over 90 percent with green defaults
Green defaults work because changing requires effort most people will not expend

faq.question: How effective are green defaults for renewable energy?
faq.answer: Extremely. When utility companies switched the default from conventional to renewable energy, participation in green tariffs rose from under 10 percent to over 90 percent. Most customers accepted the green default without even noticing the change.

faq.question: Do green defaults face political opposition?
faq.answer: Sometimes. Critics frame them as government overreach or hidden cost increases if renewable energy costs more. Transparent communication about the default and easy opt-out mechanisms reduce opposition while maintaining high uptake.
